corrections.finding: Source says one virgin queen remains 'eventually'; the text puts the young queen going on as queen at the same time as the departure, and names her 'young' where the source says one of the developing queens remains.
corrections.fixed_text: A honey bee colony swarms as it is crowding, its population growing with no room to grow in its nest, its queen's mandibular pheromone thinning through it, open cells for laying running short, with more nectar and pollen and longer days: the old queen goes out with some 50 to 70 percent of the workers, and the parent colony goes on with some 30 to 50 percent, all its brood and several queens developing in their cells, one of them in time going on as its queen. A colony is-not stable-forming here as one, and it opens as two, a social abundancing, each society going on forward.

corrections.finding: 'At one moment' and 'at its new home' are stronger than the source: the source gives a build-up (quorum, then thorax warming to 95 F, takeoff taking almost twice as long when slowed), and says nothing of the branch or arrival at a new home. 'One site' is unclear (reads as a place in the cluster, not a candidate site). '15 or more scouts' is 15 or more bees in the source. 'Much more slowly' for lift-off is stronger than 'almost twice as long'.
corrections.fixed_text: A swarm's moving begins as 15 or more bees stand at one of the sites together; scouts then scramble through the cluster pressing their vibrating thoraxes against other bees, and each bee's thorax warms to about 35 °C before the swarm lifts off, a five-site test bringing a quorum much more slowly and a lifting off almost twice as long. The swarm's parity changes across this warming and lifting, from now-existing in its cluster to next-existing in flight, a whole society warming and going.
